draft.title: Simplifying surds
card: A surd is simplified when no square factor (other than 1) is left under the root. Square numbers are 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49 and so on.
Split the number under the root into a square factor and another factor. Then use \(\sqrt{ab} = \sqrt{a} \times \sqrt{b}\) and take the square root of the square factor.
Use the largest square factor, so you finish in one step. Example: \(\sqrt{50} = \sqrt{25} \times \sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}\).

If you use a smaller square factor, the surd is not finished. \(\sqrt{72} = \sqrt{4} \times \sqrt{18} = 2\sqrt{18}\), and \(\sqrt{18}\) still has the factor 9, so this needs another step. The largest square factor of 72 is 36, giving \(6\sqrt{2}\).
draft.remember: Find the largest square factor, take its root outside, and leave no square factor inside.

a.why: The largest square factor of 48 is 16, so \(\sqrt{48} = \sqrt{16} \times \sqrt{3} = 4\sqrt{3}\). The option \(2\sqrt{12}\) is equal in value, but 12 still has the square factor 4, so it is not simplified.
a.clue: Which square number, 4 or 16, is the largest that divides 48?

b.q: Priya simplifies \(\sqrt{200}\) and writes \(\sqrt{200} = 2\sqrt{50}\). What is the correct simplest form?
b.why: The largest square factor of 200 is 100, so \(\sqrt{200} = \sqrt{100} \times \sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2}\). Priya's \(2\sqrt{50}\) is equal in value, but 50 still has the square factor 25, so it is not finished.
b.clue: Check whether the number left under the root still has a square factor.
